Special Condition (TFG):
[[File:Specialconditioncounters.jpg|thumb|250px|Assorted Special Condition markers]]
A '''Special Condition''' refers to any of a group of lasting effects that are sometimes applied to a Pokémon figure in the [[Pokémon Trading Figure Game]] and [[Pokémon Duel]]. Special Conditions are removed when the figure leaves the field. A Pokémon figure can only have one Special Condition at a time; when it receives a new Special Condition the old one is removed.

In the TFG, a Pokémon with a Special Condition is marked by a marker which is attached to the figure. Different Special Conditions have different markers. Two markers are included with each figure that is capable of inflicting a Special Condition. 

==List of Special Conditions==
Only four Special Conditions were fully implemented in the TFG, but all of them are present in Pokémon Duel.

===Paralyzed===
[[File:TFGParalyzedMarker.png|thumb|60px|A paralyzed marker]]
When a paralyzed Pokémon figure enters a battle, one of its non-Miss Attacks becomes a Miss, counting multiple wheel segments with the same name as being the same Attack. In the TFG, the Attack that will become a Miss is declared by the figure's user each time before it's spun. In Pokémon Duel, the Attack with the smallest total wheel piece size is chosen automatically; if multiple Attacks tie for the smallest total size, one is chosen at random at the start of each battle.

Paralyzed was introduced to the TFG with the first set, {{TFG|Next Quest}}.

===Poisoned===
[[File:TFGPoisonMarker.png|thumb|60px|A poisoned marker]]
In battles, the damage of a poisoned Pokémon's White and Gold Attacks is reduced by 20. This effect is applied after other effects such as {{TFG|Trainer card}}s, [[Pokémon_Duel#Plates|Plates]], and move effects.

Poisoned was introduced to the TFG with the first set, {{TFG|Next Quest}}.

===Asleep===
An asleep Pokémon can't make an MP move, activate its Ability, attack opponents, or tag allies. While asleep, the Pokémon doesn't block other Pokémon from passing through it, and it cannot help to surround opposing Pokémon. Asleep Pokémon will wake up after being attacked by an opponent or tagged by an ally. (Pokémon can choose to tag an adjacent ally rather than battling an opponent; similar to battling, tagging ends a player's turn.)

Asleep was supposed to be introduced to the TFG with the {{TFG|Groundbreakers}} expansion set.

===Confused===
When a confused Pokémon figure enters battle, it is spun normally. Before applying the result, the figure is turned counter-clockwise to the next wheel segment, which is the final spin result.

Confused was supposed to be introduced to the TFG with the {{TFG|Groundbreakers}} expansion set.

===Burned===
Burned is identical to Paralyzed, with the additional effect of reducing the damage of a Pokémon's White and Gold Attacks by 10 in battles.

Burned was never implemented in the TFG, although the {{TFG ID|Next Quest|X Accuracy|7}} trainer card mentions Misses caused by this Special Condition.

===Frozen===
Frozen is identical to Asleep, with the additional effect of turning all of a Pokémon's Attacks into Miss.

Frozen was never implemented in the TFG, although the {{TFG ID|Black Star Promo|Manaphy|6}} figure mentions that a Frozen Pokémon cannot move, similar to a Pokémon with the Asleep condition.

===Noxious===
Noxious is identical to Poisoned, except that damage is reduced by 40 instead of 20.

'''Training Center''' (Japanese: '''トレーニングセンター''' ''Training Center'') is a building on [[Carmonte Island]] where the player can practice playing the game. The building was first made accessible in version 2.0.0, which was released on November 10, 2016. The quests were changed and the player's progress reset in version 5.0.10, which was released on March 1, 2018.

Team Match:
'''Team Match''' (Japanese: '''チームマッチ''' ''Team Match'') {{OBP|event|Duel}}s are a type of competition in [[Pokémon Duel]] where players select one of three teams represented by figures and contribute to its success by earning Team Points from [[Time Booster]]s. Players may select their team during the event or preregister in the days leading up to it by selecting special icons on the home screen. While registering, [[Luca]] will suggest that the player allow him to assign them a random team. During the event an icon also allows current Team Match results to be viewed. Selecting a team causes the players home menu background to change to a series of team appropriate colors. [[League Match]] matchmaking is done between players of different teams with both players' teams being displayed before the duel. All Time Boosters and Enhancement Boosters obtained during the event open in half the time they usually require even if they are opened after the end of the event. In addition to the notable rewards listed below, the rewards also include various {{OBP|Enhancement|Duel}} figures as well as Gems. ==Team Points== [[File:Duel Team Point.png|thumb|x75px|A Team Point]] '''Team Points''' (Japanese: '''チームポイント''' ''Team Points'') are obtained by opening Time Boosters during the event, this includes any Boosters acquired before it begins. The total Team Points earned by a team's players make up its final rank and players obtain rewards throughout the event as they earn more points. Periodically during the event the teams' standings are calculated and multipliers are assigned to each one, with teams that are lagging behind in total points receiving larger multipliers. Time Booster:
'''Time Boosters''' (Japanese: '''タイムトレボ''' ''Time Trebo'') are a type of item exclusive to [[Pokémon Duel]]. They were added in version 1.3.0. They may contain various figures, enhancements, and starting in version 7.0.0, materials. Time Boosters open after a certain amount of time has passed or can be opened with Gems. By purchasing a 3-Day Duel Boost, players are able to open multiple Time Boosters at once. Starting in version 7.0.0, playing [[League Match]]es causes active Booster timers to go down by one hour up to 20 times a day. ==Currently available Time Boosters== Time Booster (Yellow) is exclusive to the tutorial. Gym Cup:
'''Gym Cups''' (Japanese: '''ジムカップ''' ''Gym Cup'') are a type of competition in [[Pokémon Duel]] in which figures of certain [[type]]s gain special gym effects. Figures whose type matches the main theme of the Gym Cup with {{mp}}0, 1, or 2 gain 1 MP and figures of a certain type which is {{DL|Type|Type_effectiveness|super effective}} against the theme type in the [[core series]] games have their White and Gold Attacks deal +20 damage. Players can set a deck to be used in Gym Cups much like they can set one for regular League Matches. The Gym Cup screen can be accessed through a button on the regular screen and contains another button to return there. By winning Gym Cup duels, the player can climb a point ladder to gain achievement rewards. In addition to the notable rewards listed below, these also include various enhancement figures as well as gems. [[Trophy (Duel)|Trophies]] are also awarded for completing certain requirements. ==Gym Boosters== Winning during a Gym Cup awards players with a Gym Booster. Similar to a [[Time Booster]], these contain figures as well as enhancements. Each consecutive win increases the number on the booster as well as the number and rarity of the rewards inside. Gym Cup participants have their Booster number indicated during Duels and matchmaking is done between players with similar Booster numbers. At any time, players may open the Booster, resetting their streak and matching them against weaker opponents in their next Duel. Dev Showdown:
[[File:Duel Developer Mask.png|thumb|70px|The Devs' Mask]] A '''Dev Showdown''' (Japanese: '''運営員マッチングイベント''' ''Staff Matching Event'') is a type of {{OBP|event|Duel}} in [[Pokémon Duel]]. During these competitions, members of the game's [[Staff of Pokémon Duel|development staff]] are inserted into the League Match rankings and compete against players during certain times. Devs can be identified by an exclusive {{OBP|Salon|Duel|mask}} they wear. Tournament (Duel):
'''Tournaments''' (Japanese: '''トーナメント''' ''Tournament'') are a type of competition in [[Pokémon Duel]]. During the preliminary round of the tournament, players can play up to 50 duels in a limited amount of time. Like other modes, players are assigned a score for tournaments which increases and decreases with their wins and losses respectively. At the end of the preliminary round, a players ranking is decided by the highest score they achieved. The top 32 players then advance to the tournament finals where matches are facilitated by the developers in a {{wp|single-elimination tournament}} to decide the final rankings. ==Golden and Silver Figures== Tournament winners are able to select a currently existing, non-{{shiny}} figure to receive Golden and Silver versions. Approximately one month after the tournament, they are given the Golden Figure and the Silver Figure is later made available through [[Time Booster]]s. Both figures can also be released at the same time. Event (Duel):
[[Pokémon Duel]] regularly hosts limited-time '''events''' for its player base which offer unique takes on the game's mechanics. By participating, players can usually gain prizes such as figures, plates, and enhancements. Each event type features a unique scoring system which is used to allocate prizes to players. Some event types appear to have been retired or heavily reworked following the game's international release in version 3.0.0. Events usually remain active until 7:59 UTC. ==Rank Match== A (Japanese: '''ランクマッチ''' ''Rank Match'') is a competition held through the [[Rank Match]] mode. To participate in a rank match players needed one of the following: 1 Lounge Ticket, 100 Coins, or 10 Gems. Starting at rank F, players increase their rank by defeating opponents and gaining points. Higher ranked opponents, each worth an increasing number of points, appear as the player climbs the ranks themselves. Like normal quests, each duel requires the player to spend energy to play, with opponents of higher rank requiring more. During certain hours of the event period, there is the possibility of the event's host appearing in the opponents list. These challengers can be dueled for the same energy as other opponents of the player's current rank but give twice as many points if they are defeated. Carnivals take place on cruise ships that dock to the left of the {{OBP|Training Center|Duel}} such as the '''S.S. Carmonte Carnival''' (Japanese: '''カーニバル・カルモンテ号''' ''Carnival Carmonte'') and the (Japanese: ''' ''' ''S.S. Burning Roger''). These Missions were related to [[League Match]]es, [[Room Match]]es, quests, Fusion, and Featured Duels. After accomplishing each mission, a random Reward can be claimed by returning to the Mission list. After completing ten Daily Missions, a '''Special Mission''' (Japanese: '''スペシャルミッション''' ''Special Mission'') is revealed. Completing this always grants players a reward from the '''Special Wheel''' (Japanese: '''スペシャルルーレット''' ''Special Roulette''). Shop (Duel):
The '''shop''' (Japanese: ''' ''' '' '') is a location on [[Carmonte Island]] in {{g|Duel}}. It is featured throughout the game's storyline, and is an important location for {{player}}s to purchase items. It is managed and operated by [[Marabelle]], with [[Tia]] as the primary salesperson. ==Mechanics== ===Claim Player Pass Figures=== After it was announced in version 7.0.14 that the game would be discontinued, all players were able to claim a figure for every 50 [[League Match]]es they had played prior to that point, additionally, players who had spent any money in the game were able to claim an additional 50 figures. Enhancement (Duel):
'''Enhancements''' (Japanese: ''' ''' '' '') are a type of item in [[Pokémon Duel]]. They are types of figures that cannot be used in Duels and are instead only used to gain in-game resources and as fusion materials. ==Rare Metal== '''Rare Metals''' (Japanese: '''レアメタル''' ''Rare Metal'') are used to grant large sums of experience points to figures. This can be used to bring them up to level 5. The higher the rarity of the Rare Metal, the more experience points it will grant. All rarities can be sold in the {{OBP|Shop|Duel}} for one Coin. Using Carmonite allows these figures to increase their level up to Level 10. Each additional Level gained in this way allows for a wheel piece to be increased by 1 while another wheel piece (that is greater than 4) is decreased by 1. The greater the rarity of the Figure, the greater the amount of Carmonite needed to level up. Carmonite could initially be sold in the {{OBP|Shop|Duel}} for 50 Coins but after it was announced in version 7.0.14 that the game would be discontinued, this sale price was doubled to 100. ==Regular Time Boosters== ==Content-restricted Time Boosters== There is no time limit to their availability. ===Time Booster (Yellow)=== This Time Booster is earned by the player during the game's tutorial and can be opened in only 3 seconds. It always contains the same figure. {| align="center" style="{{roundy|10px}}; text-align:center; border: 2px solid #{{blue color light}}; background: #{{moon color}};" |- style="background-color:#fff; vertical-align:top" | style="{{roundy|5px}}; width:70px" | {{fig|104|Pikachu|Rare}} |} ===Time Booster (Metallic)=== This Time Booster is used to distribute Silver Figures matching the Golden Figure selected by winners of {{OBP|Tournament|Duel|Tournaments}}. {| align="center" style="{{roundy|10px}}; text-align:center; border: 2px solid #{{blue color light}}; background: #{{moon color}};" |- style="background-color:#fff; vertical-align:top" | style="{{roundy|5px}}; width:70px" | {{fig|648|Dawn Wings Necrozma|UX|DawnWingsNecrozma}} |} ==Gym Boosters== {{main|Gym Cup}} These Time Boosters are available during certain [[Gym Cup]]s and gain better contents as a player's win streak increases. Their contents are the same as the Locked Booster with the addition of certain figures which also serve as Duel Wins Rewards during the event. ==Promotional Time Boosters== Periodically, special Time Boosters become available. These Boosters differ from their regular counterparts by their specialized contents and are only available for a certain period of time, often related to an in-game promotion or a real world holiday. Like regular Time Boosters, they require a certain amount of time to pass or equivalent amount of Gems to be spent in order to be opened and usually contain {{OBP|Enhancement|Duel|Enhancements}} as well as figures. During [[Team Match]]es, the Team Points they contain are derived from their unlock requirements in the same way as regular Boosters. ===Time Booster (Red)=== This Time Booster featured figures which are part of an evolutionary line, with related figures guaranteed to be received at the same time. ====October 18 to 24, 2016====

'''Gems''' are the premium currency in [[Pokémon Duel]]. They can be purchased with real money from the Gem Counter run by [[Marabelle]] at the {{OBP|Shop|Duel}}.

Each pack of Gems has a point value that is deducted from a 50000 point pool. Gems cannot be purchased if the player does not have enough points and the pool is reset at the beginning of every month. This serves to limit the amount of money that players can spend in the game.

'''The Roger family''' (Japanese: '''ロジャーファミリー''' ''Roger family''), also known as '''the Rogers''', is a [[Villainous team|villainous organization]] in [[Pokémon Duel]]. It has three known members: [[Brenda]], {{OBP|Joe|Duel}}, and [[Don Roger]], its leader.

The Roger family is immensely wealthy, owning "practically half" of [[Carmonte Island]], where Pokémon Duel takes place. The group is notorious for using shady methods to acquire rare and powerful Pokémon Figure Game (PFG) figures. It has also resorted to methods such as sabotage, kidnapping, and coercion to achieve its ends. The group has a large amount of members, enough to manage figure maintenance for the entire PFG World Championships. Of the members seen, Joe and Brenda address Don Roger as "Boss", while he addresses them by their names and refers to them as his "subordinates".

The organization's motto is "win ugly, lose pretty".

==Plot==
Prior to the events of Pokémon Duel, {{OBP|Sharon|Duel}}'s father invented the PFG League Match system, but he then became involved in a dispute with the Roger family, and lost. As a result, the Roger family took his idea, leaving Sharon's family with none of the profits. Some time later, the Roger family took part in organizing the PFG World Championships, and was put in charge of figure maintenance.

During the championships, Don Roger has Joe and Brenda investigate the Gemini AI devices "[[Carlo]]" and "[[Another]]" - two unique advanced AI that were included among the devices issued to every player. Roger seeks to acquire the two devices, with the stated goal of using them to eliminate AI from PFG, as he saw the use of AI as invalidating player skill, ruining the game he loved.

Joe encounters the player and [[Luca]] in [[Atlantis]], and is able to determine that they hold the two devices. To facilitate an approach, the Roger family has Joe replace the hotel's owner, and leverages their control of figure maintenance to insert sabotaged chips into many players' figures - causing the figures' spins to always land on "miss" wedges. However, Joe is unable to defeat the player, and passes the task to Brenda, the owner of [[Olivia Palace]]. She is also unsuccessful, leading Don Roger to intervene personally.

Don Roger challenges the player to a duel as the owner of [[The Volcano]], wagering Carlo to be taken by the winner - but Roger is defeated by the player. As a backup plan, he has Joe kidnap Luca's sister [[Tia]] in order to coerce his cooperation, offering to return Tia in exchange for Carlo and Another. Some time afterwards, the previously-dormant personality of Another awakens in Luca's device, and it negotiates for Tia's release, in exchange for helping Roger achieve his plan to change PFG. However, now without a bartering chip, the Roger family is unable to influence Luca and Another's actions - and Another starts to push Luca on his own path.

After this turn of events, Don Roger re-evaluates his stance, and finds that the player's passion for PFG is key to shaping the game's future. As such, he pivots the organization to support instead of impede the player's endeavors going forward.
